cloze.text: The ___ is the gradient function of a curve, and the ___ is the steepness of a line or curve at a point.
A ___ is a point where the gradient is zero and the tangent is horizontal, while a ___ is the straight line that just touches a curve at one point.

frames: The gradient function of a curve, giving the tangent gradient at every point, is the ___.
The steepness of a line or curve at a point, equal to the gradient of the tangent there, is the ___.
A point where the gradient is zero and the tangent is horizontal is a ___.

wordBank.gloss: dy/dx, the gradient function of a curve: it gives the tangent gradient at every point and is found by differentiating.
The steepness of a line or curve at a point. For a curve it changes from point to point and equals the gradient of the tangent there.
The straight line that just touches a curve at one point and has the same gradient as the curve at that point.
A point where dy/dx = 0 and the tangent is horizontal. It may be a maximum, a minimum or a point of inflexion - a sign test decides.
A straight line joining two points on a curve. Its gradient is an average gradient, and it becomes the tangent as the two points close in.
A point where the curve changes its bending direction. A stationary inflexion, like y = x^3 at x = 0, has dy/dx = 0 but is neither a maximum nor a minimum.
